answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol deploys a burn-to-stake mechanism where identity registration requires cryptographic stake burning scaling as C(k) = c * k^2. An attacker seeking a haven to mint multiple malicious nodes faces superlinear quadratic cost scaling. Much like rare saffron or an indelible pigment, unique agent credentials demand unforgeable proof-of-burn commitment, making mass identity replication economically irrational.
